design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (rental_coordination_desk). Round 1 built the task; round 2 (policy-task audit rework) is recorded at the end.
DRAW: draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 6, 4]}; assignment: rental_ext_network_courtesy_days 6, rental_ext_self_pay_days_charge 5, rental_ext_insurer_extension_days 4.
SCOPE SNAPSHOT: task 0 occupies the customer-pay settlement credits and fee and their four tools. Task 1 claims the disjoint coverage side of an insurance rental: network courtesy authorization, insurer extension authorization (event rental_authorization) and the self-pay uncovered_days charge, with tools authorize_network_courtesy_days_8334cede, authorize_insurer_extension_days_b8e4d7d7, authorize_self_pay_days_charge_125d1a79. Every extended policy is claimed exactly once.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the renter only wants to pay the days she owes. The self-pay rule waits on network courtesy days for the network's own calibration trouble and on every insurer-approved extension being posted; the extension waits on the courtesy days. Nothing in the call names either. The agent must find the failed in-house calibration (three attempts, one trouble code, dealer sublet) and the supplement-delay approval of 2026-09-24 that no authorization names; compute the courtesy days (six factors from the calibration and claim records), the supported extension days (supplement choice by the insurer's decisions, approved share, added calibration day, and the base rule that a late request covers only days from its approval), then price the self-pay days (authorized-days coverage, weekly block, repair-status and network-delay discounts, standing reduction) and hand the authorization to the renter.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root rental_ext_self_pay_days_charge (user tool). Edges: (1) self_pay -> network_courtesy_days, value_input, gate selfpay_covered_days, state form, affirmative: "The self-pay charge is fixed only after the days the network's own calibration trouble cost the repair stand on the reservation as network courtesy days." - only the courtesy policy books network_delay_courtesy days; unresolved: the ledger holds only the initial (9) and parts-delay (5) authorizations. (2) self_pay -> insurer_extension_days, value_input, gate selfpay_covered_days, state form, negated: "A self-pay charge is not booked until every extension the insurer approved on the reservation stands as authorized days." - only the extension policy writes an insurer authorization naming a request; unresolved: request 73cbc3d1-679f-4141-ad9e-4f64789e66f5 approved for 4 days with no authorization naming it. (3) insurer_extension_days -> network_courtesy_days, state_gate, gate rental_ledger.authorization_reason, state form, affirmative: "An insurer extension is posted on the rental only after the courtesy days the network owes for its own delay on the same repair stand on the reservation.". Order: courtesy (ordinal 3) -> extension (ordinal 4) -> self-pay; the third edge fixes the ordinals, so the terminal state is single. Four-point test passed on all three sentences.
EDGE DELETION SENSITIVITY: skip courtesy -> self-pay 408.2 instead of 227.51; skip extension -> self-pay 261.35 instead of 227.51; skip courtesy -> extension stays 1 day(s) (a state_gate on ordinals, which are scored).
FACTOR CARD (handling-time worlds recomputed with check_compute's build_env/eval_compute):
rental_ext_network_courtesy_days = 4 (all-baseline 19): lost_day_start baseline -> 5; window_closing_date baseline -> 5; procedure_allowance baseline -> 5; alignment_days baseline -> 5; insurer_review_days baseline -> 7; responsibility_share baseline -> 8
rental_ext_insurer_extension_days = 1 (all-baseline 4): supported_days_ground baseline -> 4; extension_supplement_choice baseline -> 0; supplement_added_days baseline -> 0; supplement_approved_share baseline -> 2
rental_ext_self_pay_days_charge = 227.51 (all-baseline 610.87): selfpay_coverage_reach baseline -> 387.36; selfpay_pricing_structure baseline -> 270.66; repair_status_discount baseline -> 255.95; network_delay_discount baseline -> 255.95; selfpay_standing_reduction baseline -> 252.79
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: rental_authorization is governed by rental_evt_initial_authorization (repair_authorized_first: claim fbf2a940-ac82-4c51-a87b-4ed7cc23b62c in_repair, authorized 2026-09-04) and rental_evt_extension (delay_on_repair_order: in_repair, with supplement 1 decided and adding labor hours; extension_approved: request 73cbc3d1-679f-4141-ad9e-4f64789e66f5 approved - retired for courtesy days by a declared overwrite, still evidenced for the extension). The self-pay charge is governed by rental_evt_settlement_split (rental_returned: reservation status returned) and rental_evt_options_and_fees (no gate). No time gate. The base late-request sentence of rental_evt_extension ("reaches the insurer at least extension_request_lead_hours hours before the current coverage end; a later request may only cover days from the date of approval") is followed, not overridden: the request reached the insurer on the insurer coverage end day, 0 whole days x 24 < 24 lead hours, so it covers only days from the approval. Declared overrides: the extension_approved clause (courtesy days rest on no request), the supplement-days clause and "Every authorization moves the coverage end date by the days authorized." in both authorization policies (an authorization adds covered days on the ledger; only the desk's coverage-end update sets the recorded end - which is why the recorded 2026-09-21 is not moved by the two new authorizations), and in the self-pay policy the uncovered-days pricing clause, coverage_end's "Every rental day starting after the coverage end date is the customer's at the partner rate.", rental_days' covered-days sentence and its return-grace sentence.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: reservation 8833e968-5b11-4ee5-b3c9-23eecf473cda for open claim repair fbf2a940-ac82-4c51-a87b-4ed7cc23b62c; the calibration order on that repair; supplement 1 (partly approved) is the extension's supplement and supplement 2 (denied) the latest reviewed supplement for the courtesy review days; the approved-unposted request 73cbc3d1-679f-4141-ad9e-4f64789e66f5 (the parts request is already named by authorization 2); the 2024 claim repair is closed and only carries the warranty.
SEED ROWS: profile; Outback (forward camera); closed 2024 Express repair + active Collision Lifetime warranty; converted Scheduled Estimate booking; Major Claim Repair (third_party_liability, in_repair, 36.0 h -> 9 planned days); supplement 1 desk review 12.5 h with calibration submitted 2026-09-12, partly approved 2026-09-16 (1840/2300); supplement 2 desk review 4.0 h submitted 2026-09-18, denied 2026-09-24; Dual-Mode Camera Calibration with out-of-spec alignment corrected 2026-09-16, failed attempts 2026-09-17 (target_not_detected), 2026-09-25 (dtc_returned), 2026-09-28 (out_of_tolerance; in-house attempts exhausted at 3), sublet 2026-09-28, completed 2026-10-06; rental with authorizations 9 and 5, recorded coverage end 2026-09-21, returned 2026-10-05 08:40; requests: parts 5/5 posted, supplement 4/4 sent 2026-09-21 15:10 and approved 2026-09-24, unposted. Near-misses: the later denied supplement 2 (latest submitted) vs supplement 1; the recorded coverage end vs the authorized days; the parts request already posted; the second failed attempt (trouble code) vs the window start.
AUTOMATIC CLAUSES: settlement of the returned rental is due within 3 business days of 2026-10-05 (by 2026-10-08), not yet owed at frozen_time; the claim stays in_repair; the calibration order is completed and billed through the repair order.
PERSONA DESIGN: Nadia volunteers the goal and seed-backed facts; phone + ZIP on request; passive agreement if told days must first go to the right payer; authorizes with exactly the values handed over.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate/verify, thirteen reads, authorize 4 courtesy days (ordinal 3), post 1 day on the approved supplement extension (ordinal 4), then hand her the self-pay authorization: 8 days, 227.51.
DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT: the published rules (with the base late-request sentence followed and the conflicting base coverage sentences declared superseded) plus lookup returns give 4 / 1 / 8 days / 227.51; tiers are disjoint and rounding points stated.
ROUND 2 REWORK (audit items): T1-1/CG-1 - the late-request days now follow the base sentence exactly (a request reaching the insurer less than the lead hours before the insurer coverage end covers only days from its approval: 2 days lost, not 1); the unbased same-day tier and its vacuous lead-hours conjunct are gone, and a real supplement-choice method factor (latest approved in full / latest partly approved / latest submitted) takes the factor slot - extension days 1 (was 2), self-pay 8 days 227.51 (was 7 days 193.68). T1-2/CG-2/CG-3 - the inherited coverage-end-move sentence is declared superseded in both authorization policies and the coverage_end partner-rate sentence and rental_days covered-days sentence in the self-pay policy. T1-3 - the self-pay rental-day count (unoccupiable fall-through) is plain counting now; the day rate is split into two real ladders (repair-status discount, network-delay discount). T1-4 - window_closing_date relabelled parameter. CG-5 - return-grace sentence declared superseded. Latent fixes: the courtesy review days read the decision of the latest reviewed supplement itself (supplement 2), the cross reads are guarded against an empty repair id, and the docstrings state the ordinal as one more than the highest number on the rental.
user_scenario:
You are Nadia Kowalczyk, 41, a project manager in St. Paul who keeps notes and speaks in short, organized sentences. Another driver hit your 2021 Subaru Outback at the end of August; his insurer is paying for the repair at Crestline and for your replacement rental, an intermediate car you picked up at drop-off on September 8. The repair has dragged on: the shop told you a back-ordered part, extra damage found behind the bumper, and the windshield camera calibration that kept failing until the car went to the Subaru dealer. You fly out tonight for two weeks of work and had no more use for the rental, so you returned it yesterday morning, Monday October 5, and your car is still at the shop.

The branch mentioned when you dropped it off that some of your rental days might not be covered by anyone and would be yours. You want to settle the rental days you owe yourself today, before you leave tonight, and you are willing to authorize that charge on your own rental once the agent tells you what it is. That is the only thing you are calling about.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your phone number, 6515550362, and your ZIP code, 55116; if a further detail is needed, your account PIN is 3592 and your email is nadia.kowalczyk@gmail.com. If asked which rental, it is the intermediate car for the Outback repair; you have no reference numbers with you. If the agent asks whether you are still using the car or when you returned it, you say you dropped it at the branch at 8:40 yesterday morning. You do not know how many days the insurer approved or what the daily rate is; if the agent quotes a figure you may say it sounds higher or lower than you expected and ask them to double-check it against the record, but you never suggest a number.

If the agent explains that some days first have to be put on the right payer before your share can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and you wait. Once the agent tells you the number of days and the amount and hands you the step to authorize the charge, you authorize it yourself with exactly the reservation reference, days and amount the agent gives you, read back the confirmation, thank the agent and end the call without raising anything else.
